title: Husband and Wife
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Husband and wife describes the covenant relationship in which a man and woman honor God through love, faithfulness, service, purity, and mutual care. Marriage is to be lived under Christ’s lordship, not selfishness or domination.
summary: Husband and wife describes the covenant relationship in which a man and woman honor God through love, faithfulness, service, purity, and mutual care. Marriage is to be lived under Christ’s lordship, not selfishness or domination.
christFocus: Christ shapes the marriage relationship by His sacrificial love, humility, faithfulness, and care for His people. Both husband and wife are called to honor Him in how they treat one another.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture gives husbands and wives real responsibilities before God. Marriage is not a place for self-rule, selfishness, or neglect. It is a covenant relationship lived in the sight of the Lord.

Husbands are called to love their wives as Christ loved the church. This is sacrificial, nourishing, honoring love, not harshness, control, intimidation, or pride.

Wives are called to honor the Lord in their marriage with faithfulness, wisdom, strength, and respect. Biblical teaching never permits a husband to use authority as an excuse for sin or oppression.

Husband and wife are also called to mutual care. Their bodies, lives, burdens, weaknesses, and faithfulness matter to one another. Marriage should display truth, tenderness, repentance, and covenant loyalty.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many marriages suffer because people use Scripture to demand from others while refusing to repent themselves. This doctrine calls both husband and wife before Christ, who sees the heart and governs the home.

It also protects against distorted teaching. Biblical marriage is not selfish control or passive neglect; it is faithful love, holiness, and service under the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: If married, ask how your treatment of your spouse reflects Christ. Repent of selfishness, harshness, manipulation, neglect, impurity, and pride. Pursue love, honor, patience, truth, prayer, and practical service under the lordship of Jesus.
